item.title: Former Texas Rangers Player Heavy Favorite to Replace Chip Roy in Congress
item.description: By Olivia Borgula, The Texas TribuneWASHINGTON — In his first-ever run for elected office, former Major League Baseball player Mark Teixeira is overpowering the field of a dozen Republicans competing to replace Rep. Chip Roy in Congress, pumping millions of his personal wealth into his campaign and locking up key endorsements, including a recent nod from President Donald Trump. Learn More Here.

item.title: Man Sues Tom Green County After Allegedly Swallowing Glass in Jail Meal
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — A civil lawsuit alleging an inmate swallowed broken glass hidden in jail food nearly four years ago remains active in Tom Green County district court, with a motion to compel scheduled for Feb. 18.Herman Tyrone Stanley III filed the suit in February 2024 against Tom Green County, the Tom Green County Jail and several Aramark entities that provide food service to the facility. Learn More Here.

item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — A crash between two vehicles in San Angelo disrupted traffic Tuesday afternoon. It happened at about 12:30 p.m. at the intersection of South Koenigheim Street and West Avenue B. Learn More Here.

item.title: Angelo State Softball Jumps to No. 2 in National Rankings
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — After a 9-1 start to the season, the Angelo State University softball team has jumped all the way to No. 2 in the NCAA Division II national rankings.The Rambelles were ranked No. 13 in the preseason poll, but they’ve leapfrogged 11 spots after only two weeks. Learn More Here.

item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — The Angelo State Rambelles will take their six-game winning streak on the road to Central Texas this week as the journey continues toward clinching a spot in the Lone Star Conference tournament. Learn More Here.

item.title: Central Bobcats Claim Another Commanding Home Victory
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — The Central Bobcats claimed yet another dominant home win on Tuesday night, this time against the Midland Bulldogs. Central led from start to finish for a 64-54 win.Central (26-5, 7-1 in district) led by as much as 21 points in the contest. The Bobcats opened up a 15-4 first-quarter lead, before Midland battled back in the second. Central struggled from beyond the arc early, but made up for it by utilizing excellent passing to find open players underneath the basket. Learn More
